title: Early Intravenous Beta-Blockers in Patients With ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Before Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised double-blind multicentre trial, 683 patients (metoprolol n = 336, placebo n = 346); CMR performed in 342 patients (54.8%).
appraisal.main_limitation: Primary end point was a surrogate (infarct size), and CMR was available in only about half of patients.
appraisal.one_line: Placebo-controlled trial of early intravenous metoprolol before primary PCI in STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Infarct size (percent of left ventricle [LV]) by CMR did not differ between the metoprolol (15.3 ± 11.0%) and placebo groups (14.9 ± 11.5%; p = 0.616).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It tests early beta-blockade in a general STEMI population and found no effect on infarct size.

title: Prasugrel Versus Ticagrelor in Patients With Acute Myocardial Infarction Treated With Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: Multicenter Randomized PRAGUE-18 Study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial, 1230 patients assigned across 14 sites.
appraisal.main_limitation: Terminated early with broad confidence intervals; primary endpoint at 7 days.
appraisal.one_line: Head-to-head randomised comparison of prasugrel and ticagrelor in primary PCI for acute MI was stopped for futility and showed no difference at 7 days.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The occurrence of the primary end point did not differ between groups receiving prasugrel and ticagrelor (4.0% and 4.1%, respectively; odds ratio, 0.98; 95% confidence interval, 0.55-1.73; P=0.939).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses a common choice of P2Y12 inhibitor in STEMI, though underpowered.

title: Extracorporeal life support during cardiac arrest and cardiogenic shock: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis; propensity matched analysis included 5 studies and 438 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: The included studies were largely observational and subject to selection bias.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of extracorporeal life support in cardiac arrest and cardiogenic shock, with survival associated with ECLS versus no ECLS or IABP.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In cardiac arrest, the use of ECLS was associated with an absolute increase of 30 days survival of 13 % compared with patients in which ECLS was not used [95 % CI 6-20 %; p < 0.001; number needed to treat (NNT) 7.7]. In cardiogenic shock, ECLS showed a 33 % higher 30-day survival compared with IABP (95 % CI, 14-52 %; p < 0.001; NNT 13).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Mechanical circulatory support in arrest and shock is widely used with little randomised evidence, so pooled estimates inform equipoise.

title: Editor's Choice- Impact of immediate multivessel percutaneous coronary intervention versus culprit lesion intervention on 1-year outcome in patients with acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock: Results of the randomised IABP-SHOCK II trial.
journal: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective analysis of a randomised trial; 451 (75%) of the total of 600 patients had multivessel coronary artery disease.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised comparison within a trial, with treatment chosen by operators.
appraisal.one_line: Post hoc analysis of IABP-SHOCK II comparing immediate multivessel PCI with culprit lesion PCI in cardiogenic shock.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The 30-day (44.9% vs. 42.3%) and 12-month (54.8% vs. 52.7%) mortality rates did not significantly differ between the two groups; 12-month mortality odds ratio 0.92, 95% confidence intervals 0.69-1.21.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It bears on the strategy later tested in CULPRIT-SHOCK and shows equipoise in multivessel PCI in shock.

title: Percutaneous Mechanical Circulatory Support Versus Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump in Cardiogenic Shock After Acute Myocardial Infarction.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised open-label multicentre trial, 48 patients (24 per arm).
appraisal.main_limitation: Very small sample; exploratory.
appraisal.one_line: Small randomised trial of Impella CP versus IABP in ventilated AMI cardiogenic shock found similar mortality.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 30 days, mortality in patients treated with either IABP or pMCS was similar (50% and 46%, respectively; hazard ratio with pMCS: 0.96; 95% confidence interval: 0.42 to 2.18; p = 0.92).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Rare randomised data on percutaneous mechanical support in cardiogenic shock.

title: Multivessel versus culprit lesion only percutaneous coronary intervention in cardiogenic shock complicating acute myocardial infarction: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
journal: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of 10 cohort studies including 6051 patients, 1194 (19.7%) with MV-PCI and 4857 (80.3%) with C-PCI.
appraisal.main_limitation: No randomised trials and probable treatment selection bias in the contributing cohorts.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of cohort studies comparing multivessel with culprit-only PCI in cardiogenic shock after myocardial infarction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Short-term mortality was 37.5% in patients undergoing MV-PCI compared with 28.8% in C-PCI patients (risk ratio 1.26, 95% confidence interval 1.12-1.41, p=0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Pooled observational signal against immediate multivessel PCI in shock, ahead of the randomised trial in this setting.

title: Contemporary Management of Cardiogenic Shock: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.

appraisal.design_and_n: Scientific statement; no sample size applies.
appraisal.main_limitation: A consensus statement from a field with few randomised interventions, so recommendations rest largely on expert opinion.
appraisal.one_line: American Heart Association scientific statement on the contemporary management of cardiogenic shock.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It sets out the current approach to cardiogenic shock, advocates regionalised systems of care and lists research priorities for the field.

title: Percutaneous short-term active mechanical support devices in cardiogenic shock: a systematic review and collaborative meta-analysis of randomized trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Collaborative meta-analysis of randomized trials; four trials randomizing 148 patients to TandemHeart or Impella (n = 77) versus control (n = 71), all with intra-aortic balloon pumping as control.
appraisal.main_limitation: Four small trials with IABP as the comparator, so the pooled sample is underpowered for mortality.
appraisal.one_line: Collaborative meta-analysis of randomised trials of percutaneous active mechanical circulatory support in cardiogenic shock.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: There was no difference in 30-day mortality (RR 1.01, 95% CI 0.70 to 1.44, P = 0.98, I2 = 0%) for active MCS compared with control.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It shows the thin randomised evidence for percutaneous MCS in cardiogenic shock and an increase in bleeding, which frames the case for larger trials.

title: Early coronary angiography in patients resuscitated from out of hospital cardiac arrest without ST-segment elevation: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of 8 studies (7 observational studies and 1 randomized control trial).
appraisal.main_limitation: Dominated by observational studies with selection bias.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis associating early angiography after non-ST-elevation cardiac arrest with lower mortality.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Short term mortality OR=0.46, 95% CI=0.36-0.56, P<0.001; long term mortality OR=0.59, 95%CI=0.44-0.74, P<0.001 with early angiography.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears on invasive management after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest without ST elevation, a decision made frequently.

title: PCI Strategies in Patients with Acute Myocardial Infarction and Cardiogenic Shock.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicenter randomized trial; 706 patients with multivessel disease, acute myocardial infarction and cardiogenic shock.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design with 30-day follow-up, and the culprit-only arm allowed staged revascularisation at the operator's discretion.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial finding that culprit-lesion-only PCI led to lower 30-day death or renal replacement therapy than immediate multivessel PCI in infarct-related cardiogenic shock.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 30 days, the composite primary end point of death or renal-replacement therapy had occurred in 158 of the 344 patients (45.9%) in the culprit-lesion-only PCI group and in 189 of the 341 patients (55.4%) in the multivessel PCI group (relative risk, 0.83; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.71 to 0.96; P=0.01).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It changes a high-mortality decision made in most patients with infarct-related cardiogenic shock and challenges routine immediate multivessel PCI.

title: Impact of Regionalization of ST-Segment-Elevation Myocardial Infarction Care on Treatment Times and Outcomes for Emergency Medical Services-Transported Patients Presenting to Hospitals With Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: Mission: Lifeline Accelerator-2.

appraisal.design_and_n: Quality-improvement programme in 12 US metropolitan regions with 132 PCI-capable hospitals and 946 EMS agencies; 10 730 patients transported.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised before-and-after design without adjustment reported in the abstract.
appraisal.one_line: A regional EMS-hospital coordination programme was followed by shorter reperfusion times and lower in-hospital mortality in STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The proportion with first medical contact to device time ≤90 minutes rose from 67% to 74% (P<0.002); in-hospital death fell from 4.4% to 2.3% (P=0.001), not apparent in non-participating hospitals.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Evidence for regionalised systems of care in STEMI.

title: Culprit Vessel-Only Versus Multivessel Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Patients With Cardiogenic Shock Complicating ST-Segment-Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Collaborative Meta-Analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of 11 nonrandomized studies and 5850 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Nonrandomised studies only, with confounding by indication.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of multivessel versus culprit-only PCI in infarct-related cardiogenic shock.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Short-term mortality OR, 1.08; 95% CI, 0.81-1.43; P=0.61 for multivessel versus culprit-only PCI.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses a contested decision in cardiogenic shock before randomised trial results.

title: Anticoagulant Use Among Patients With End-Stage Renal Disease Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: An Analysis From the National Cardiovascular Data Registry.

appraisal.design_and_n: CathPCI Registry analysis of n=71 675 patients with end-stage renal disease receiving bivalirudin or UFH.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational registry data with confounding by indication and in-hospital outcomes only.
appraisal.one_line: Registry analysis associating bivalirudin with lower bleeding and mortality than heparin in dialysis-dependent PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In hospital bleeding (7.0% versus 9.5%; adjusted odds ratio,0.82; 95% confidence interval, 0.76-0.87) lower with bivalirudin.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides data in a population largely excluded from antithrombotic trials.

title: Position paper for the organization of ECMO programs for cardiac failure in adults.

appraisal.design_and_n: Position paper without a stated sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Expert opinion with limited supporting evidence, as the paper itself notes.
appraisal.one_line: Position paper on organisation of ECMO programmes for adult cardiac failure.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Sets out programme and team structures for ECMO in refractory cardiogenic shock and cardiac arrest.

title: Impact of treatment delay on mortality in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) patients presenting with and without haemodynamic instability: results from the German prospective, multicentre FITT-STEMI trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Analysis of the prospective multicentre FITT-STEMI trial, n = 12 675 STEMI patients transported by emergency medical service and treated with primary PCI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational time-to-treatment association with possible confounding by indication.
appraisal.one_line: Contact-to-balloon delay was linked to excess mortality, most steeply in STEMI with cardiogenic shock.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In CS patients with no OHCA, every 10-min treatment delay resulted in 3.31 additional deaths in 100 PCI-treated patients, versus 0.34 in haemodynamically stable patients (P < 0.0001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports prioritising speed of reperfusion in shock, relevant to shock systems of care.

title: Multivessel Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Patients With ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction With Cardiogenic Shock.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Nationwide prospective KAMIR-NIH registry; 659 patients treated by multivessel PCI (n = 260) or IRA-only PCI (n = 399).
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational data with selection of patients for multivessel PCI despite adjustment methods.
appraisal.one_line: Registry analysis of multivessel versus infarct-related-artery-only PCI in STEMI with cardiogenic shock.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The risk of all-cause death and non-IRA repeat revascularization was significantly lower in the multivessel PCI group than in the IRA-only PCI group (21.3% vs. 31.7%; hazard ratio: 0.59; 95% confidence interval: 0.43 to 0.82; p = 0.001; and 6.7% vs. 8.2%; hazard ratio: 0.39; 95% confidence interval: 0.17 to 0.90; p = 0.028, respectively).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses a decision where randomised evidence in shock is limited, and is hypothesis-generating for complete revascularisation in shock.

title: Delayed Coronary Obstruction After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective international registry of 18 centres, November 2005 to December 2016; 38 DCO cases from a total of 17,092 TAVR procedures.
appraisal.main_limitation: Retrospective case collection without a denominator for timing and subject to reporting bias.
appraisal.one_line: Multicentre registry description of delayed coronary obstruction after TAVR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: 38 DCO (incidence 0.22%) cases were identified from a total of 17,092 TAVR procedures. DCO occurred more commonly after valve-in-valve procedures (0.89% vs. 0.18%; p < 0.001) and if self-expandable valves were used during the index procedure (0.36% vs. 0.11% balloon expandable; p < 0.01). The overall in-hospital death rate was 50% (n = 19).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Characterises a rare, highly lethal complication relevant to coronary access planning after TAVR.

title: Mortality and morbidity in acutely ill adults treated with liberal versus conservative oxygen therapy (IOTA): a systematic review and meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials; 25 randomised controlled trials enrolled 16 037 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Mixed acute populations; few trials in myocardial infarction specifically.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of liberal versus conservative oxygen therapy in acutely ill adults including MI and cardiac arrest populations.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A liberal oxygen strategy increased mortality in-hospital (relative risk [RR] 1·21, 95% CI 1·03-1·43, I2=0%, high quality), at 30 days (RR 1·14, 95% CI 1·01-1·29, I2=0%, high quality), and at longest follow-up (RR 1·10, 95% CI 1·00-1·20, I2=0%, high quality).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs oxygen use in acute MI and post-arrest care.

title: Oxygen therapy in ST-elevation myocardial infarction.

appraisal.design_and_n: Pre-specified analysis of a randomized trial; 2807 patients (1361 oxygen, 1446 ambient air).
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup of a trial not powered separately for STEMI.
appraisal.one_line: Pre-specified DETO2X-AMI analysis of supplemental oxygen in STEMI patients treated with PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The pre-specified primary composite endpoint occurred in 6.3% (86 of 1361) of patients allocated to oxygen compared to 7.5% (108 of 1446) allocated to ambient air [hazard ratio (HR) 0.85, 95% confidence interval (95% CI) 0.64-1.13; P = 0.27].
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports abandoning routine oxygen in normoxaemic STEMI.

title: Epinephrine Versus Norepinephrine for Cardiogenic Shock After Acute Myocardial Infarction.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective, double-blind, multicenter, randomized study; Fifty-seven patients were randomized into 2 study arms.
appraisal.main_limitation: Very small sample and haemodynamic primary endpoint.
appraisal.one_line: Double-blind randomised comparison of epinephrine and norepinephrine in cardiogenic shock after MI, stopped early.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: For the main safety endpoint, the observed higher incidence of refractory shock in the epinephrine group (10 of 27 [37%] vs. norepinephrine 2 of 30 [7%]; p = 0.008) led to early termination of the study.
appraisal.why_it_matters: The only randomised data on first-line vasopressor choice in AMI-related shock.

title: One-Year Outcomes after PCI Strategies in Cardiogenic Shock.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 706 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Mortality difference at 1 year was not statistically significant; open-label.
appraisal.one_line: One-year outcomes of culprit-lesion-only versus immediate multivessel PCI in AMI with cardiogenic shock.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 1 year, death had occurred in 172 of 344 patients (50.0%) in the culprit-lesion-only PCI group and in 194 of 341 patients (56.9%) in the multivessel PCI group (relative risk, 0.88; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.76 to 1.01).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Guides revascularisation strategy in a high-mortality setting.

title: Early Versus Standard Care Invasive Examination and Treatment of Patients With Non-ST-Segment Elevation Acute Coronary Syndrome.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial (VERDICT, NCT02061891); 2147 patients randomised to angiography within 12 hours or within 48 to 72 hours.
appraisal.main_limitation: The high-risk finding comes from a subgroup interaction and its confidence interval includes 1.
appraisal.one_line: Very early invasive strategy within 12 hours did not improve long-term outcomes over standard invasive care in non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome, with a signal in high-risk patients.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary end point occurred in 296 (27.5%) in the very early group and 316 (29.5%) in the standard care group (hazard ratio, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.78-1.08). In patients with GRACE score >140 the hazard ratio was 0.81 (95% CI, 0.67-1.01; P value for interaction=0.023).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs the timing of invasive management in NSTE-ACS and the case for early angiography in the highest-risk patients.

title: Intraaortic Balloon Pump in Cardiogenic Shock Complicating Acute Myocardial Infarction: Long-Term 6-Year Outcome of the Randomized IABP-SHOCK II Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Long-term follow-up of a multicentre randomised open-label trial (NCT00491036); 600 patients, follow-up complete for 591.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design, and the trial pre-dates current shock practice and devices.
appraisal.one_line: Six-year follow-up of IABP-SHOCK II shows no difference in mortality with intra-aortic balloon pump in cardiogenic shock after myocardial infarction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Mortality was not different between the IABP and the control group (66.3% versus 67.0%; relative risk, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.88-1.11; P=0.98).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Confirms the neutral long-term effect of IABP and the very high late mortality in infarct-related shock.

title: Unloading the Left Ventricle Before Reperfusion in Patients With Anterior ST-Segment-Elevation Myocardial Infarction.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre randomised exploratory safety and feasibility trial (NCT03000270); 50 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small exploratory trial not powered for efficacy.
appraisal.one_line: Pilot trial found Impella CP unloading with 30 minutes of delayed reperfusion feasible in anterior STEMI without prohibitive safety signals.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular event rates were not statistically different between the U-IR versus U-DR groups (8% versus 12%, respectively, P=0.99). Mean infarct size was 15±12% versus 13±11% (P=0.53).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides the safety basis for a pivotal trial of unloading before reperfusion, a new direction in STEMI care.

title: Impella Support for Acute Myocardial Infarction Complicated by Cardiogenic Shock.

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective registry analysis matched to randomised trial controls (NCT03313687); 372 Impella patients identified, 237 matched to 237 from IABP-SHOCK II.
appraisal.main_limitation: Retrospective registry patients matched to historical trial controls leave residual confounding and era effects.
appraisal.one_line: Matched comparison with IABP-SHOCK II patients found no 30-day mortality difference with Impella in infarct-related cardiogenic shock and more bleeding and vascular complications.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: There was no significant difference in 30-day all-cause mortality (48.5% versus 46.4%, P=0.64). Severe or life-threatening bleeding (8.5% versus 3.0%, P<0.01) and peripheral vascular complications (9.8% versus 3.8%, P=0.01) occurred significantly more often in the Impella group.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds observational evidence on a widely used device with little randomised data, supporting the need for a randomised trial.

title: The Evolving Role of the Cardiac Catheterization Laboratory in the Management of Patients With Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.

appraisal.design_and_n: Scientific statement; narrative review of observational and trial evidence, no pooled sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Evidence base is mainly observational case series with selection bias, as the statement notes.
appraisal.one_line: AHA scientific statement reviews coronary disease prevalence in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest and the emerging use of early angiography and VA-ECMO-facilitated resuscitation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Sets out the position of a major society on catheterisation and mechanical support after cardiac arrest while randomised trials are pending.

title: Left Ventricular Unloading During Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Patients With Cardiogenic Shock.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 17 observational studies; 3,997 patients, 1,696 (42%) with concomitant unloading.
appraisal.main_limitation: Only observational studies, with confounding by indication and mostly intra-aortic balloon pump as the unloading method.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of observational studies associated left ventricular unloading during VA-ECMO with lower mortality in cardiogenic shock.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Mortality was lower in patients with (54%) versus without (65%) left ventricular unloading while on VA-ECMO (risk ratio: 0.79; 95% confidence interval: 0.72 to 0.87; p < 0.00001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Summarises the best available evidence on unloading strategies where no randomised data exist.

title: Coronary Angiography after Cardiac Arrest without ST-Segment Elevation.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre randomised trial (COACT, NTR4973); 552 patients randomised.
appraisal.main_limitation: Delayed angiography strategy was angiography after neurological recovery, and the trial was not powered for small differences.
appraisal.one_line: Immediate coronary angiography was not better than delayed angiography for 90-day survival after resuscitated cardiac arrest without ST-segment elevation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 90 days, 176 of 273 patients (64.5%) in the immediate angiography group and 178 of 265 patients (67.2%) in the delayed angiography group were alive (odds ratio, 0.89; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.62 to 1.27; P = 0.51).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Challenges routine immediate angiography in cardiac arrest without STEMI, a decision made in a high-mortality setting.

title: Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Older Patients With ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction and Cardiogenic Shock.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Observational analysis of 317,728 encounters with STEMI and shock, of which 111,901 (35%) were adults aged 75 years or older.
appraisal.main_limitation: In-hospital outcome only, administrative data and confounding by selection for PCI.
appraisal.one_line: National inpatient database analysis associating PCI with lower in-hospital mortality in older adults with STEMI and cardiogenic shock.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Utilizing PS matching methods, PCI was associated with a lower risk of in-hospital mortality across quintiles of propensity score (Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio: 0.48; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.45 to 0.51).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Relevant to the exclusion of older patients from invasive shock care.

title: Effect of remote ischaemic conditioning on clinical outcomes in patients with acute myocardial infarction (CONDI-2/ERIC-PPCI): a single-blind randomised controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: International single-blind randomised controlled trial; 5401 patients randomly allocated (2569 control and 2546 remote ischaemic conditioning analysed).
appraisal.main_limitation: Sham conditioning was used at UK sites only, and the analysis excluded patients after randomisation.
appraisal.one_line: CONDI-2/ERIC-PPCI found no improvement in cardiac death or heart failure hospitalisation at 12 months with remote ischaemic conditioning before primary PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The Kaplan-Meier-estimated frequencies of cardiac death or hospitalisation for heart failure were 220 (8·6%) patients in the control group and 239 (9·4%) in the remote ischaemic conditioning group (hazard ratio 1·10 [95% CI 0·91-1·32], p=0·32 for intervention versus control).
appraisal.why_it_matters: A large neutral trial that closes a long-running line of adjunctive STEMI cardioprotection research.

title: Cardiogenic Shock Classification to Predict Mortality in the Cardiac Intensive Care Unit.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective single-centre cohort (Mayo Clinic CICU, 2007 to 2015), 10,004 unique patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Retrospective staging from admission data at a single centre.
appraisal.one_line: Application of the SCAI shock classification to a large cardiac ICU cohort showing graded hospital mortality by stage.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Unadjusted hospital mortality in SCAI stages A through E was 3.0%, 7.1%, 12.4%, 40.4%, and 67.0% (p < 0.001), respectively. Cardiac arrest was associated with higher mortality (adjusted odds ratio: 3.99; 95% confidence interval: 3.27 to 4.86; p < 0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports the SCAI classification as a risk-stratification tool that could underpin shock trials and systems of care.

title: Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: a registry study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective Paris-region registry of 13 191 OHCAs from May 2011 to January 2018; 525 patients given extracorporeal-CPR.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational registry with possible residual confounding and selection into extracorporeal-CPR.
appraisal.one_line: Population-based registry comparison of survival with and without extracorporeal CPR in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Survival was 8% in 525 patients given extracorporeal-CPR and 9% in 12 666 patients given conventional-CPR (P = 0.91). By adjusted multivariate analysis, extracorporeal-CPR was not associated with hospital survival [odds ratio (OR), 1.3; 95% confidence interval (95% CI), 0.8-2.1; P = 0.24].
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds population-level data on ECPR effectiveness ahead of randomised evidence.

title: 2019 American Heart Association Focused Update on Advanced Cardiovascular Life Support: Use of Advanced Airways, Vasopressors, and Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation During Cardiac Arrest: An Update to the American Heart Association Guidelines for Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation and Emergency Cardiovascular Care.

appraisal.design_and_n: Guideline focused update summarising published evidence; no sample size applies.
appraisal.main_limitation: The abstract gives no recommendation classes or levels, so positions cannot be taken from it.
appraisal.one_line: The 2019 AHA focused update revises recommendations on advanced airways, vasopressors and extracorporeal CPR in cardiac arrest.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Sets the guideline position on ECPR and post-arrest care within the cardiac arrest domain.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Low-Dose Colchicine after Myocardial Infarction.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised, double-blind trial; 4745 patients enrolled within 30 days of MI (2366 colchicine, 2379 placebo), median follow-up 22.6 months.
appraisal.main_limitation: The effect was driven by stroke and urgent angina hospitalisation, with no clear effect on cardiovascular death or MI.
appraisal.one_line: COLCOT found low-dose colchicine reduced the composite of ischaemic cardiovascular events after recent MI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary end point occurred in 5.5% of the patients in the colchicine group, as compared with 7.1% of those in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.77; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.61 to 0.96; P = 0.02). Pneumonia was reported as a serious adverse event in 0.9% of the patients in the colchicine group and in 0.4% of those in the placebo group (P = 0.03).
appraisal.why_it_matters: First large outcome trial of an anti-inflammatory drug started early after MI, with direct implications for post-MI secondary prevention guidelines.

title: The Evolving Landscape of Impella Use in the United States Among Patients Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention With Mechanical Circulatory Support.

appraisal.design_and_n: Premier Healthcare Database, 48 306 patients undergoing PCI with MCS at 432 hospitals between January 2004 and December 2016; 4782 (9.9%) received Impella.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational administrative data with unmeasured confounding by indication.
appraisal.one_line: Large US hospital database analysis of Impella use trends, variation and outcomes in PCI with mechanical circulatory support.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: After adjustment for the propensity score, and accounting for clustering of patients by hospitals, Impella use was associated with death: odds ratio, 1.24 (95% CI, 1.13-1.36); bleeding: odds ratio, 1.10 (95% CI, 1.00-1.21); and stroke: odds ratio, 1.34 (95% CI, 1.18-1.53).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Documents rapid uptake and wide hospital variation in Impella use despite limited randomised evidence in PCI.

title: Recognition and Initial Management of Fulminant Myocarditis: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.

appraisal.design_and_n: Scientific statement; no sample size applies.
appraisal.main_limitation: Consensus statement based on limited evidence; the abstract cites no quantitative data.
appraisal.one_line: AHA scientific statement sets out resources and pathways for recognising and managing fulminant myocarditis, including mechanical circulatory support.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Guides systems of care for shock, including referral for extracorporeal and percutaneous support.

title: Initial Invasive or Conservative Strategy for Stable Coronary Disease.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 5179 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Primary outcome sensitive to the myocardial infarction definition; patients with left main disease and reduced ejection fraction were excluded.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised comparison of an initial invasive versus conservative strategy in stable coronary disease with moderate or severe ischaemia.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 6 months, the cumulative event rate was 5.3% in the invasive-strategy group and 3.4% in the conservative-strategy group (difference, 1.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.8 to 3.0); at 5 years, the cumulative event rate was 16.4% and 18.2%, respectively (difference, -1.8 percentage points; 95% CI, -4.7 to 1.0). Results were similar with respect to the key secondary outcome. The incidence of the primary outcome was sensitive to the definition of myocardial infarction; a secondary analysis yielded more procedural myocardial infarctions of uncertain clinical importance. There were 145 deaths in the invasive-strategy group and 144 deaths in the conservative-strategy group (hazard ratio, 1.05; 95% CI, 0.83 to 1.32).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Directly informs the most common revascularisation decision in chronic coronary syndromes.

title: Management of Coronary Disease in Patients with Advanced Kidney Disease.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 777 patients with advanced chronic kidney disease and moderate or severe ischaemia.
appraisal.main_limitation: Shorter median follow-up of 2.2 years and a high-risk population with few events beyond death.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised comparison of invasive and conservative strategies in stable coronary disease with advanced kidney disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At a median follow-up of 2.2 years, a primary outcome event had occurred in 123 patients in the invasive-strategy group and in 129 patients in the conservative-strategy group (estimated 3-year event rate, 36.4% vs. 36.7%; adjusted hazard ratio, 1.01; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.79 to 1.29; P = 0.95)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Fills a population excluded from earlier revascularisation trials and shows higher stroke with the invasive strategy.

title: Venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation to rescue sepsis-induced cardiogenic shock: a retrospective, multicentre, international cohort study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective, multicentre, international cohort: 82 patients with septic shock who received VA-ECMO at five academic ECMO centres, compared with 130 controls.
appraisal.main_limitation: Retrospective design with unmeasured confounding, small numbers and non-contemporaneous controls.
appraisal.one_line: Retrospective international cohort comparing VA-ECMO with no ECMO in refractory sepsis-induced cardiogenic shock.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: After propensity score weighting, ECMO remained associated with improved survival (51% vs 14%, adjusted RR for mortality 0·57, 95% CI [0·35-0·93]; p=0·0029).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides the first comparative signal for VA-ECMO in septic cardiogenic shock, supporting a randomised trial.

title: Randomized Pilot Clinical Trial of Early Coronary Angiography Versus No Early Coronary Angiography After Cardiac Arrest Without ST-Segment Elevation: The PEARL Study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised pilot trial; 99 patients, terminated prematurely.
appraisal.main_limitation: Underpowered and stopped early.
appraisal.one_line: Pilot randomised trial of early coronary angiography after cardiac arrest without ST elevation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary end point of efficacy and safety was not different between the 2 groups (55.1% versus 46.0%; P=0.64)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds to equipoise on early angiography after resuscitation.

title: Left Ventricular Unloading Is Associated With Lower Mortality in Patients With Cardiogenic Shock Treated With Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation: Results From an International, Multicenter Cohort Study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre observational cohort, 686 patients at 16 centres in 4 countries; 255 matched pairs.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational propensity matching with possible unmeasured confounding and selection of unloading by centre practice.
appraisal.one_line: In a propensity-matched cohort of VA-ECMO cardiogenic shock, left ventricular unloading with Impella was associated with lower 30-day mortality and more complications.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In the matched cohort, left ventricular unloading was associated with lower 30-day mortality (hazard ratio, 0.79 [95% CI, 0.63-0.98]; P=0.03). Severe bleeding occurred in 98 (38.4%) versus 45 (17.9%).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs the unresolved question of LV unloading during VA-ECMO that randomised trials are intended to address.

title: Advanced reperfusion strategies for patients with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest and refractory ventricular fibrillation (ARREST): a phase 2, single centre, open-label, randomised controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Phase 2, single-centre, open-label randomised trial; 30 randomised (15 vs 15).
appraisal.main_limitation: Single centre, 30 patients, stopped at first interim analysis.
appraisal.one_line: ARREST: early ECMO-facilitated resuscitation improved survival to discharge in refractory VF out-of-hospital cardiac arrest in a stopped-early single-centre trial.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Survival to hospital discharge was 1 of 15 (7%; 95% credible interval 1.6-30.2) with standard ACLS versus 6 of 14 (43%; 21.3-67.7) with early ECMO (risk difference 36.2%, 3.7-59.2; posterior probability of ECMO superiority 0.9861).
appraisal.why_it_matters: First randomised signal for ECPR in refractory VF, ahead of larger trials.

title: Predictive Value of the Residual SYNTAX Score in Patients With Cardiogenic Shock.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Secondary analysis of the randomised CULPRIT-SHOCK trial; 587 patients with residual SYNTAX score available.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc and observational association; residual score is post-treatment and confounded by anatomy and haemodynamic state.
appraisal.one_line: In CULPRIT-SHOCK, residual SYNTAX score was independently associated with 30-day and 1-year mortality, and complete revascularisation was achieved in a minority.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Complete revascularisation was achieved in 75 (25.2%; 95% CI: 20.3% to 30.5%) with multivessel PCI and 27 (9.3%; 95% CI: 6.2% to 13.3%) with culprit-only PCI. Residual SYNTAX score was associated with 30-day mortality (adjusted odds ratio per 10 units: 1.49; 95% CI: 1.11 to 2.01) and 1-year mortality (adjusted odds ratio per 10 units: 1.52; 95% CI: 1.11 to 2.07).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Quantifies the prognostic cost of incomplete revascularisation in infarct-related shock, relevant to the culprit-only strategy.

title: Risk Stratification Among Survivors of Cardiac Arrest Considered for Coronary Angiography.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: INTCAR registry, 2,508 patients successfully resuscitated after cardiac arrest.
appraisal.main_limitation: Registry data with possible self-fulfilling withdrawal of care and no assessment of angiography benefit.
appraisal.one_line: In an international cardiac arrest registry, accumulation of unfavourable features predicted poor survival among patients considered for coronary angiography.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The presence of any 3 or more unfavorable features predicted <40% survival. Presence of the 3 strongest risk factors together or ≥6 unfavorable features predicted a ≤10% chance of survival to discharge.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears on selection for invasive management after cardiac arrest.

title: Invasive Management of Acute Myocardial Infarction Complicated by Cardiogenic Shock: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.

appraisal.design_and_n: Scientific statement; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Statement rests on limited randomised data, noting that a mortality benefit from MCS in AMICS has not been established in randomised trials.
appraisal.one_line: AHA scientific statement on interventional management of AMI complicated by cardiogenic shock, covering revascularisation and MCS use.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Sets US practice positions on revascularisation and MCS in AMI-CS.

title: Kidney Transplant List Status and Outcomes in the ISCHEMIA-CKD Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Post hoc analysis of the randomised ISCHEMIA-CKD trial (n = 777); 194 patients (25%) listed for transplant; NCT01985360.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc subgroup; wide intervals.
appraisal.one_line: ISCHEMIA-CKD analysis: an invasive strategy did not improve outcomes in patients listed for kidney transplant.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Adjusted hazard ratios for the primary outcome with invasive versus conservative strategy were 0.91 (95% CI: 0.54-1.54) in listed and 1.03 (95% CI: 0.78-1.37) in not listed patients (pinteraction= 0.68).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses pre-transplant coronary evaluation in advanced CKD.

title: Milrinone as Compared with Dobutamine in the Treatment of Cardiogenic Shock.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised double-blind trial, 192 participants (96 per group).
appraisal.main_limitation: Underpowered for modest differences in mortality, as the confidence intervals are wide.
appraisal.one_line: A double-blind trial found no significant difference between milrinone and dobutamine in cardiogenic shock.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A primary outcome event occurred in 47 participants (49%) in the milrinone group and in 52 participants (54%) in the dobutamine group (relative risk, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.69 to 1.19; P = 0.47). In-hospital death was 37% and 43% (relative risk, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.60 to 1.21).
appraisal.why_it_matters: First randomised comparison of the two commonest inotropes in cardiogenic shock; neither is shown to be superior.

title: Angiography after Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest without ST-Segment Elevation.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised multicentre trial, 554 randomised, 530 analysed (265 per group).
appraisal.main_limitation: The delayed group included selective angiography, so the comparison is of strategies rather than of angiography itself.
appraisal.one_line: TOMAHAWK found no benefit from immediate coronary angiography after resuscitated cardiac arrest without ST-segment elevation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 30 days, 143 of 265 patients (54.0%) in the immediate-angiography group and 122 of 265 patients (46.0%) in the delayed-angiography group had died (hazard ratio, 1.28; 95% CI, 1.00 to 1.63; P = 0.06).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Argues against routine immediate angiography in this population, a common decision in invasive management after cardiac arrest.

title: Management and Outcomes of Cardiogenic Shock in Cardiac ICUs With Versus Without Shock Teams.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Critical Care Cardiology Trials Network, 24 CICUs, 1,242 shock admissions.
appraisal.main_limitation: Centre-level observational comparison with only 24 centres and residual confounding.
appraisal.one_line: Multicentre network data associated cardiac ICUs with shock teams with lower risk-adjusted mortality in cardiogenic shock.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The presence of a shock team was independently associated with lower CICU mortality (23% vs 29%; adjusted OR: 0.72; 95% CI: 0.55-0.94; P = 0.016).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Systems-of-care evidence on shock teams and MCS use.

title: Effect of Moderate Hypothermia vs Normothermia on 30-Day Mortality in Patients With Cardiogenic Shock Receiving Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial at 20 French centres, 374 randomised and 334 analysed (168 hypothermia, 166 normothermia).
appraisal.main_limitation: Wide confidence interval and the authors describe the findings as inconclusive; 30 of 31 secondary outcomes were inconclusive.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of early moderate hypothermia during VA-ECMO for cardiogenic shock did not significantly reduce 30-day mortality.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 30 days, 71 patients (42%) in the moderate hypothermia group had died vs 84 patients (51%) in the normothermia group (adjusted odds ratio, 0.71 [95% CI, 0.45 to 1.13], P = .15; risk difference, -8.3% [95% CI, -16.3% to -0.3%]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Randomised evidence on supportive care during VA-ECMO in cardiogenic shock, an area with few trials.

title: Effect of Intra-arrest Transport, Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation, and Immediate Invasive Assessment and Treatment on Functional Neurologic Outcome in Refractory Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Single-centre randomised trial, 256 patients (124 invasive, 132 standard), stopped for futility.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single centre, stopped before planned sample size of 285 and possibly underpowered, as the authors state.
appraisal.one_line: Prague OHCA trial of an invasive strategy with intra-arrest transport and ECPR did not significantly improve neurologically favourable survival.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 180 days, 39 patients (31.5%) vs 29 (22.0%) survived with good neurologic outcome (odds ratio [OR], 1.63 [95% CI, 0.93 to 2.85]; difference, 9.5% [95% CI, -1.3% to 20.1%]; P = .09).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Randomised evidence on ECPR in refractory cardiac arrest, pointing to a possible benefit that larger trials must test.

title: Mechanical Left Ventricular Unloading in Patients Undergoing Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: ELSO registry analysis of 12,734 VA-ECMO patients, of whom 3,399 (26.7%) received mechanical unloading.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational registry data with confounding by indication, as unloaded patients were sicker at baseline.
appraisal.one_line: Registry comparison of mechanical left ventricular unloading with IABP or pVAD during peripheral VA-ECMO.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Mechanical unloading was associated with lower in-hospital mortality (56.6% vs 59.3%, P = 0.006; adjusted OR [aOR]: 0.84; 95% CI: 0.77-0.92; P < 0.001), with more cannula site bleeding (aOR: 1.25; 95% CI: 1.11-1.40) and hemolysis (aOR: 1.27; 95% CI: 1.03-1.57).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It bears on the unresolved question of routine LV unloading during VA-ECMO, where randomised evidence is scarce.

title: Criteria for Defining Stages of Cardiogenic Shock Severity.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Cardiogenic Shock Working Group registry of 17 hospitals, 3,455 patients enrolled between 2016 and 2021.
appraisal.main_limitation: Registry derivation without external validation reported in the abstract.
appraisal.one_line: Registry-derived formal criteria for SCAI cardiogenic shock stages.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Mortality was 35% for the total cohort. Systolic blood pressure, lactate level, alanine transaminase level, and systemic pH were significantly associated with mortality and used to define each stage; baseline and maximum stages were significantly associated with mortality (n = 1,890).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Operational stage definitions would standardise shock trial enrolment and risk stratification.

title: Escalating and De-escalating Temporary Mechanical Circulatory Support in Cardiogenic Shock: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.

appraisal.design_and_n: Scientific statement from the American Heart Association; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Expert consensus in the absence of randomised evidence, so suggestions rest on limited data.
appraisal.one_line: AHA scientific statement gives pragmatic guidance on selection, escalation and weaning of temporary mechanical circulatory support in cardiogenic shock, in the absence of randomised data.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides a reference framework for escalation and de-escalation of MCS in AMI and heart failure shock (D2) and highlights evidence gaps for the register.

title: Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Mitral Valve Repair in Patients With Severe Mitral Regurgitation and Cardiogenic Shock.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry analysis; 3,797 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational, with device success defined post hoc and subject to survivor and selection bias.
appraisal.one_line: STS/ACC TVT Registry analysis found device success of TEER in cardiogenic shock with mitral regurgitation was associated with lower 1-year mortality.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 1 year after TEER, device success was associated with significantly lower all-cause mortality (34.6% vs 55.5%; adjusted HR: 0.49; 95% CI: 0.41-0.59; P < 0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Hypothesis-generating data for TEER in shock (D4, D2), where no randomised trial exists.

title: Coronary angiography after cardiac arrest without ST-elevation myocardial infarction: a network meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and network meta-analysis; 16 studies (six RCTs, ten non-randomised studies).
appraisal.main_limitation: DerSimonian-Laird pooling with high heterogeneity overall and mixed randomised and non-randomised designs; search ended July 2022.
appraisal.one_line: Network meta-analysis found that the apparent survival benefit of early coronary angiography after cardiac arrest without ST elevation was driven by non-randomised studies and was not seen in randomised trials.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Meta-analyses showed a statistically significant increase in survival after early CAG compared with selective CAG in the overall analysis [OR: 1.40, 95% confidence interval (CI): (1.12-1.76), P < 0.01, I2 = 68%]; this effect was lost in the subgroup analysis of RCTs [OR: 0.89, 95% CI: (0.73-1.10), P = 0.29, I2 = 0%].
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears on routine early angiography after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest without STEMI (D2), where guideline practice is still debated.

title: Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in the Therapy of Cardiogenic Shock: Results of the ECMO-CS Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre randomised academic trial; 117 patients analysed (58 immediate VA-ECMO, 59 no immediate VA-ECMO).
appraisal.main_limitation: Small sample with wide confidence intervals; 39% crossover to VA-ECMO in the conservative group.
appraisal.one_line: ECMO-CS randomised patients with rapidly deteriorating or severe cardiogenic shock to immediate VA-ECMO or an early conservative strategy and found no difference in the composite outcome.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The composite primary end point occurred in 37 (63.8%) and 42 (71.2%) patients in the immediate VA-ECMO and the no early VA-ECMO groups, respectively (hazard ratio, 0.72 [95% CI, 0.46-1.12]; P=0.21).
appraisal.why_it_matters: One of few randomised comparisons of VA-ECMO strategy in cardiogenic shock (D2) and informs escalation decisions.

title: Early Extracorporeal CPR for Refractory Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre randomised controlled trial in the Netherlands; 160 patients randomised, 70 to extracorporeal CPR and 64 to conventional CPR.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small trial with 26 patients excluded after randomisation for not meeting inclusion criteria, limiting power and precision.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of early extracorporeal CPR versus conventional CPR in refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest found no difference in favourable neurological survival.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 30 days, 14 patients (20%) in the extracorporeal-CPR group were alive with a favorable neurologic outcome, as compared with 10 patients (16%) in the conventional-CPR group (odds ratio, 1.4; 95% confidence interval, 0.5 to 3.5; P = 0.52).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Tests an increasingly adopted resource-intensive strategy against standard care and bears directly on guideline positions for ECPR.

title: Influence of Culprit Lesion Intervention on Outcomes in Infarct-Related Cardiogenic Shock With Cardiac Arrest.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry and randomised trial analysis of 1,015 patients, of whom 550 (54.2%) had cardiac arrest.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis with limited power for interaction testing.
appraisal.one_line: Analysis of cardiac arrest in infarct-related cardiogenic shock within the CULPRIT-SHOCK population.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: One-year death was 53.8% vs 50.4% (P = 0.29) in patients with and without cardiac arrest; cardiac arrest was an independent predictor of 1-year mortality (HR: 1.27; 95% CI: 1.01-1.59).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports culprit-lesion-only PCI in shock regardless of cardiac arrest.

title: Outcomes of transcatheter aortic valve replacement in patients with cardiogenic shock.

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry cohort of 309 505 TAVR patients, of whom 5006 (1.6%) presented with cardiogenic shock.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational registry with heterogeneous shock definitions and no comparison to alternative treatments such as balloon valvuloplasty or medical therapy.
appraisal.one_line: STS/ACC TVT registry analysis of balloon-expandable TAVR in patients presenting with cardiogenic shock.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In propensity-matched analysis, cardiogenic shock was associated with higher in-hospital (9.9% vs. 2.7%), 30-day (12.9% vs. 4.9%) and 1-year (29.7% vs. 22.6%) mortality. In the landmark analysis after 30 days, 1-year mortality was similar (hazard ratio [HR] 1.07, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.95-1.21).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides outcome estimates in a population excluded from pivotal trials and informs the shock-TAVR decision.

title: Arrhythmia and Death Following Percutaneous Revascularization in Ischemic Left Ventricular Dysfunction: Prespecified Analyses From the REVIVED-BCIS2 Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Secondary analysis of a randomised trial; 700 patients, 347 assigned to PCI plus OMT and 353 to OMT alone.
appraisal.main_limitation: Secondary analysis of a trial with open-label allocation; arrhythmia ascertainment depends on device availability.
appraisal.one_line: Prespecified REVIVED-BCIS2 analysis of arrhythmia and death after PCI in ischaemic left ventricular dysfunction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: All-cause death or aborted sudden death occurred in 144 patients (41.6%) in the PCI group and 142 patients (40.2%) in the OMT group (hazard ratio, 1.03 [95% CI, 0.82-1.30]; P=0.80).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Shows PCI did not reduce fatal arrhythmia in ischaemic cardiomyopathy, informing revascularisation in this population.

title: Extracorporeal Life Support in Infarct-Related Cardiogenic Shock.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 420 patients randomised and 417 included in final analyses, 209 in the ECLS group and 208 in the control group.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label trial with planned early revascularisation; the findings may not extend to selected phenotypes.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of extracorporeal life support in infarct-related cardiogenic shock found no reduction in 30-day mortality.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 30 days, death from any cause had occurred in 100 of 209 patients (47.8%) in the ECLS group and in 102 of 208 patients (49.0%) in the control group (relative risk, 0.98; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.80 to 1.19; P = 0.81).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Challenges routine use of VA-ECMO in infarct-related shock and bleeding and vascular complications were more frequent with ECLS.

title: Venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation in patients with infarct-related cardiogenic shock: an individual patient data meta-analysis of randomised trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Individual patient data meta-analysis of four randomised trials (n=567 patients; 284 VA-ECMO, 283 control).
appraisal.main_limitation: Few trials with open-label allocation and variable crossover and ECMO protocols.
appraisal.one_line: Individual patient data meta-analysis of VA-ECMO versus control in infarct-related cardiogenic shock.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: There was no significant reduction of 30-day death rate with the early use of VA-ECMO (OR 0·93; 95% CI 0·66-1·29); major bleeding was higher (OR 2·44; 95% CI 1·55-3·84).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Pools the randomised evidence on VA-ECMO in infarct-related shock and supports a careful review of indications.

title: Long-Term Outcomes of Cardiogenic Shock Complicating Myocardial Infarction.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Population-based retrospective cohort, 9,789 consecutive patients with AMI-CS from 135 centres, 2009 to 2019.
appraisal.main_limitation: Retrospective administrative data without shock severity staging or device-specific detail.
appraisal.one_line: Population-based Ontario cohort describing long-term outcomes of cardiogenic shock complicating MI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A total of 2,961 patients (30.2%) died in the hospital, and 4,004 (40.9%) died by 1 year. Mortality at 5 years was 58.9%. Among survivors to discharge, 3,244 (47.5%) were readmitted to the hospital within 1 year, and 1,047 (15.3%) died within 1 year.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides long-term benchmarks and shows minimal improvement over a decade, relevant to shock systems and post-discharge care.

title: Early Left Ventricular Unloading or Conventional Approach After Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation: The EARLY-UNLOAD Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 116 patients randomised, all completing the trial.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small sample, with 29 patients (50%) in the conventional group crossing over to rescue unloading.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of early left ventricular unloading versus conventional approach in cardiogenic shock on VA-ECMO.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 30 days, all-cause death had occurred in 27 (46.6%) patients in the early group and 26 (44.8%) patients in the conventional group (hazard ratio, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.59-1.74]; P=0.942).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Tests routine LV unloading in VA-ECMO, a widely used but unproven strategy.

title: 2023 American Heart Association Focused Update on Adult Advanced Cardiovascular Life Support: An Update to the American Heart Association Guidelines for Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation and Emergency Cardiovascular Care.

appraisal.design_and_n: Guideline focused update; no sample size applicable.
appraisal.main_limitation: The abstract does not describe the strength of evidence or specific recommendations, and notes limited data on diversity, equity and inclusion.
appraisal.one_line: The 2023 AHA focused update revises adult advanced cardiovascular life support recommendations, including coronary angiography and extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: A new guideline update that sets practice for post-arrest invasive management and ECPR in the cardiac arrest domain.

title: Cardiogenic Shock in Older Adults: A Focus on Age-Associated Risks and Approach to Management: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.

appraisal.design_and_n: Scientific statement; no sample size applicable.
appraisal.main_limitation: Consensus-based, and older adults have been largely excluded from the underlying trials.
appraisal.one_line: AHA scientific statement summarises risk assessment and management of cardiogenic shock in older adults and argues against age alone guiding decisions.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses a population excluded from shock trials and relevant to device and advanced therapy eligibility.

title: Microaxial Flow Pump or Standard Care in Infarct-Related Cardiogenic Shock.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: 360 patients randomised, 355 analysed (179 microaxial-flow-pump, 176 standard care).
appraisal.main_limitation: Moderate sample size with a confidence interval close to unity, selection for patients without hypoxic brain injury, and a higher rate of complications.
appraisal.one_line: DanGer Shock found that routine microaxial flow pump use in STEMI-related cardiogenic shock lowered 180-day mortality, with more device-related adverse events.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Death from any cause occurred in 82 of 179 patients (45.8%) in the microaxial-flow-pump group and in 103 of 176 patients (58.5%) in the standard-care group (hazard ratio, 0.74; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.55 to 0.99; P = 0.04). A composite safety end-point event occurred in 43 patients (24.0%) in the microaxial-flow-pump group and in 11 (6.2%) in the standard-care group (relative risk, 4.74; 95% CI, 2.36 to 9.55).
appraisal.why_it_matters: The first randomised mortality benefit for mechanical circulatory support in infarct-related cardiogenic shock.

title: Ventricular septal defect complicating acute myocardial infarction: diagnosis and management. A Clinical Consensus Statement of the Association for Acute CardioVascular Care (ACVC) of the ESC, the European Association of Percutaneous Cardiovascular Interventions (EAPCI) of the ESC and the ESC Working Group on Cardiovascular Surgery.

appraisal.design_and_n: Consensus statement and state-of-the-art review; no sample size applicable.
appraisal.main_limitation: Consensus is built on observational evidence because no randomised trials are available.
appraisal.one_line: Clinical consensus statement on post-MI ventricular septal defect, a rare complication with very high mortality and no randomised evidence.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Sets out management options and research priorities for a high-mortality complication with no trial evidence.

title: Serial Shock Severity Assessment Within 72 Hours After Diagnosis: A Cardiogenic Shock Working Group Report.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre CSWG registry, 3,268 patients (57% HF-CS; 27% MI-CS).
appraisal.main_limitation: Registry data from selected shock centres without randomised comparisons.
appraisal.one_line: Cardiogenic Shock Working Group registry analysis of serial SCAI stage changes over 72 hours.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 24 hours, >50% of stages B and C patients worsened, but 86% of stage D patients stayed at stage D. Within 24 hours, unadjusted mortality rates of patients with any SCAI stage worsening or improving were 44.6% and 34.2%, respectively.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports serial staging within 24 hours for risk stratification and trial enrolment.

title: Temporary mechanical circulatory support in infarct-related cardiogenic shock: an individual patient data meta-analysis of randomised trials with 6-month follow-up.

appraisal.design_and_n: Nine reports of randomised controlled trials (n=1114 patients); four trials (n=611 patients) of VA-ECMO and five trials (n=503 patients) of left ventricular unloading devices.
appraisal.main_limitation: Pools heterogeneous devices and trials, and the subgroup finding is not a randomised comparison.
appraisal.one_line: IPD meta-analysis finds early routine mechanical circulatory support did not reduce 6-month mortality in infarct-related cardiogenic shock overall, with benefit in a selected subgroup and more bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: No significant benefit of early unselected MCS use on 6-month mortality was noted (HR 0·87 [95% CI 0·74-1·03]; p=0·10). Patients with ST-elevation cardiogenic shock without risk of hypoxic brain injury had a reduction in mortality with MCS use (0·77 [0·61-0·97]; p=0·024). Major bleeding (odds ratio 2·64 [95% CI 1·91-3·65]) and vascular complications (4·43 [2·37-8·26]) were more frequent with MCS use than with control.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Frames patient selection for mechanical support in infarct-related shock, alongside the DanGer Shock result.

title: Microaxial Flow Pump Use and Renal Outcomes in Infarct-Related Cardiogenic Shock: A Secondary Analysis of the DanGer Shock Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified secondary analysis of a randomized open-label trial; 355 adult patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Secondary analysis of an open-label trial; predictors are associations only.
appraisal.one_line: Prespecified DanGer Shock analysis shows more acute kidney injury and renal replacement therapy with the microaxial pump, without loss of the mortality benefit.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: RRT was used in 75 (42%) and 47 (27%) patients, respectively (P<0.01); mAFP use was associated with higher rates of RRT, even when accounting for competing risk of death (subdistribution hazard, 1.67 [1.18-2.35]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Quantifies a principal harm of microaxial flow pump support and identifies device-specific modifiable factors such as suction events and pump speed.

title: Mixed Cardiogenic Shock: A Proposal for Standardized Classification, a Hemodynamic Definition, and Framework for Management.

appraisal.design_and_n: Consensus-style primer; no patient-level analysis.
appraisal.main_limitation: Proposal rests on registry and trial data without prospective validation of the thresholds.
appraisal.one_line: Proposed classification and haemodynamic definition of mixed cardiogenic shock with a management framework.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Standardised phenotyping of mixed shock could allow registries and trials to enrol and analyse these patients consistently.

title: Coronary artery bypass grafting vs. percutaneous coronary intervention in severe ischaemic cardiomyopathy: long-term survival.

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry cohort with inverse probability of treatment weighting; 2042 patients (1451 CABG, 591 PCI).
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational data with residual confounding, and the stroke estimate is very imprecise.
appraisal.one_line: Registry analysis in severe ischaemic cardiomyopathy associated CABG with lower long-term mortality than PCI after weighting.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Adjusted hazard ratio 0.59, 95% confidence interval 0.45-0.79, P = .001 for long-term mortality with CABG versus PCI; peri-procedural stroke aOR 19.6, 95% CI 4.21-91.6.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs revascularisation choice in low ejection fraction, where trial evidence is sparse.

title: Transcatheter Valve Replacement in Severe Tricuspid Regurgitation.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomized international trial; 400 patients, 2:1 allocation (267 valve replacement, 133 control).
appraisal.main_limitation: Industry-funded open-label trial with a composite driven by quality-of-life measures, and no mortality or hospitalisation advantage.
appraisal.one_line: TRISCEND II found transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement superior to medical therapy on a hierarchical composite driven by symptoms and quality of life, with more bleeding and pacemaker implantation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 1 year, the win ratio favoring valve replacement was 2.02 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.56 to 2.62; P<0.001). Severe bleeding occurred in 15.4% of the valve-replacement group and in 5.3% of the control group (P = 0.003); new permanent pacemakers were implanted in 17.4% and 2.3%, respectively (P<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Pivotal randomized evidence for transcatheter tricuspid replacement, with a clear safety trade-off.

title: Treating Older Patients in Cardiogenic Shock With a Microaxial Flow Pump: Is it DANGERous?
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Exploratory secondary analysis of a randomized open-label trial; 355 patients with STEMI-related cardiogenic shock.
appraisal.main_limitation: Exploratory, with few older patients and a wide interval in the older group.
appraisal.one_line: DanGer Shock age analysis suggests the mortality benefit of the microaxial pump may not extend to patients aged 77 years or older.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In patients <77 years, a reduced 180-day mortality was observed in patients randomized to the mAFP (OR: 0.45; 95% CI: 0.28-0.73; P = 0.001), opposed to patients aged ≥77 years (OR: 1.52; 95% CI: 0.57-4.08; P = 0.40), P for interaction = 0.028.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Directly relevant to patient selection for microaxial support in older people, a population underrepresented in the trial.

title: Evolution of Critical Care Cardiology: An Update on Structure, Care Delivery, Training, and Research Paradigms: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.

appraisal.design_and_n: Scientific statement; expert consensus.
appraisal.main_limitation: Expert opinion without systematic evidence grading.
appraisal.one_line: AHA scientific statement updating the structure, staffing and research agenda of the cardiac intensive care unit.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Sets organisational and research directions for critical care cardiology and shock care.

title: Early Intra-Aortic Balloon Support for Heart Failure-Related Cardiogenic Shock: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicenter randomized trial; 53 patients randomized to IABP and 48 to standard care.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small trial stopped at interim analysis with crossover from standard care to IABP.
appraisal.one_line: Altshock-2 stopped for futility, with no significant improvement in survival or bridging to transplant from early IABP in heart failure cardiogenic shock.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint was reached in 43 patients (81%) in the IABP group and 36 patients (75%) in the control group (HR: 0.72; 95% CI: 0.31-1.68; P = 0.45).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Rare randomized evidence in non-infarct cardiogenic shock, where mechanical support practice is driven by observational data.

title: Outcomes after fractional flow reserve-guided percutaneous coronary intervention versus coronary artery bypass grafting (FAME 3): 5-year follow-up of a multicentre, open-label, randomised trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre randomised trial in three-vessel disease; 757 assigned to PCI and 743 to CABG.
appraisal.main_limitation: Noninferiority of PCI was not shown at 1 year and the 5-year comparison is not powered for individual components.
appraisal.one_line: FAME 3 five-year results show no significant difference in death, stroke or MI between FFR-guided PCI and CABG, with more MI and repeat revascularisation with PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 5 years, there was no significant difference in the composite of death, stroke, or myocardial infarction between the two groups, with 119 (16%) events in the PCI group and 101 (14%) in the CABG group (hazard ratio 1·16 [95% CI 0·89-1·52]; p=0·27).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs shared decision-making between PCI and CABG in three-vessel disease.

title: Evolution of Critical Care Cardiology: An Update on Structure, Care Delivery, Training, and Research Paradigms: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Scientific statement; expert consensus.
appraisal.main_limitation: Expert opinion without systematic evidence grading.
appraisal.one_line: AHA scientific statement updating the structure, staffing and research agenda of the cardiac intensive care unit (JACC publication).
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Sets organisational and research directions for critical care cardiology and shock care.

title: Immediate versus staged complete revascularisation during index admission in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and multivessel disease (OPTION-STEMI): a multicentre, non-inferiority, open-label, randomised trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Open-label randomised noninferiority trial at 14 hospitals in South Korea, 994 patients (498 immediate, 496 staged).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label with a wide noninferiority margin (HR 1·42) relative to observed event rates, so the result is inconclusive rather than showing equivalence.
appraisal.one_line: OPTION-STEMI did not show immediate complete revascularisation to be noninferior to staged complete revascularisation during the index admission in STEMI with multivessel disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint occurred at 1 year in 65 patients (13%) in the immediate group and 53 patients (11%) in the staged group (HR 1·24 [95% CI 0·86-1·79]; pnon-inferiority=0·24).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses the timing of non-culprit PCI in STEMI, a question left open by existing complete revascularisation trials.

title: Effect of ECMO Flow Variations on Pulmonary Capillary Wedge Pressure in Patients With Cardiogenic Shock.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective single-centre interventional study of 80 patients with stepwise flow variation from 2 to 4 L/min.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single centre, short physiological observation after stabilisation, with no clinical outcomes.
appraisal.one_line: Prospective interventional study of stepwise VA-ECMO flow changes and pulmonary capillary wedge pressure in cardiogenic shock.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: PCWP decreased in 29 patients (36%), remained stable in 46 (58%), and increased in only 5 (6%), despite a concomitant rise in LV afterload.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Challenges the assumption that higher ECMO flow raises left atrial pressure, which informs routine LV unloading decisions.

title: DanGer shock criteria and outcomes in acute myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock treated with Impella: the J-PVAD registry.

appraisal.design_and_n: Nationwide registry of 3975 AMI-CS patients treated with Impella from 2020 to 2023.
appraisal.main_limitation: Descriptive registry without a comparator group, so benefit of Impella in non-eligible patients cannot be assessed.
appraisal.one_line: J-PVAD registry describes how many Impella-treated AMI-CS patients met DanGer shock criteria and their 30-day mortality.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Eligible STEMI-CS accounted for 35.6% of all AMI-CS cases, with a 30-day mortality of 37.6%. Non-eligible STEMI-CS patients had lower mortality (27.6%). Thirty-day mortality was 51.3% in OHCA, 39.8% in MC, and 33.3% in NSTEMI-CS groups.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Shows the gap between trial-eligible and treated populations for microaxial flow pump use.

title: Part 4: Systems of Care: 2025 American Heart Association Guidelines for Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation and Emergency Cardiovascular Care.

appraisal.design_and_n: Guideline; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Abstract does not state recommendation classes or levels for individual items.
appraisal.one_line: 2025 AHA guideline chapter on cardiac arrest systems of care, including ECPR, transport to specialised arrest centres and performance measurement.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Sets the US guideline position on systems of care and ECPR relevant to shock and arrest pathways.

title: Part 11: Post-Cardiac Arrest Care: 2025 American Heart Association Guidelines for Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation and Emergency Cardiovascular Care.

appraisal.design_and_n: Guideline; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Abstract does not state recommendation classes or levels, which must be taken from the full text.
appraisal.one_line: 2025 AHA guideline on post-cardiac arrest care, covering blood pressure, oxygen and temperature goals, PCI, mechanical circulatory support and neuroprognostication.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Updates US guidance on invasive coronary management and mechanical support after resuscitation, a common source of ESC and AHA discordance.

title: Sex-Specific Microaxial Flow Pump Use and Outcomes in Infarct-Related Cardiogenic Shock in the DanGer Shock Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified secondary analysis of a randomised trial, 355 patients (74 women, 281 men); 179 randomised to mAFP.
appraisal.main_limitation: Only 74 women, with no significant treatment-by-sex interaction, so differential benefit cannot be established.
appraisal.one_line: Prespecified sex analysis of DanGer Shock found higher mortality in women with STEMI-CS and less apparent benefit from the microaxial flow pump, without a significant interaction.
