appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Women had significantly higher 180-day all-cause mortality (64.9% vs 48.8%; P = 0.015); women HR: 1.01 [95% CI: 0.58-1.79] vs men HR: 0.66 [95% CI: 0.47-0.93] for mAFP treatment (P value for interaction = 0.18).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears on selection for microaxial flow pump support in women with infarct-related cardiogenic shock.

title: Levosimendan to Facilitate Weaning From ECMO in Patients With Severe Cardiogenic Shock: The LEVOECMO Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 11 French ICUs, 205 patients (levosimendan n = 101; placebo n = 104).
appraisal.main_limitation: Mixed aetiologies including postcardiotomy shock, and the sample was modest for mortality outcomes.
appraisal.one_line: LEVOECMO found early levosimendan did not improve successful VA-ECMO weaning in severe cardiogenic shock.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Within 30 days, 69 of 101 patients (68.3%) had a successful ECMO weaning in the levosimendan group compared with 71 of 104 (68.3%) in the placebo group (risk difference, 0.0% [95% CI, -12.8% to 12.7%]; subdistribution hazard ratio, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.74-1.39]; P = .92).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Randomised evidence against a commonly used adjunct for weaning from VA-ECMO.

title: Complete revascularization timing in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and multivessel disease with heart failure: the OPTION-STEMI trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified subgroup analysis of a randomised trial, 994 patients, of whom 329 (33.1%) had heart failure at admission.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis with a borderline interaction P value, in a trial that did not meet its noninferiority aim.
appraisal.one_line: Prespecified OPTION-STEMI subgroup suggests immediate complete revascularisation was worse than staged in STEMI patients with heart failure at admission, but not in those without.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Immediate complete revascularization was associated with a higher incidence of the primary endpoint than staged in patients with heart failure (22.8% vs 13.3%; HR 1.79; 95% CI 1.05-3.04), but not in those without (8.0% vs 9.5%; HR 0.84; 95% CI .50-1.40); P = .043 for interaction.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Suggests Killip class should inform the timing of non-culprit PCI in STEMI.

title: Immediate vs Delayed Coronary Angiography After Cardiac Arrest Without ST-Segment Elevation: 5-Year Outcomes From the COACT Randomized Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Long-term follow-up of an open-label randomised trial at 19 Dutch centres; 5-year data for 514 of 552 patients (261 immediate, 253 delayed).
appraisal.main_limitation: Follow-up by telephone interview, and the landmark analysis was nonprespecified and exploratory.
appraisal.one_line: Five-year COACT follow-up shows no survival difference between immediate and delayed coronary angiography after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest without ST elevation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Five years after the index hospitalization, 143 patients (54.8%) were alive in the immediate angiography group, and 131 patients (51.8%) were alive in the delayed angiography group (HR: 0.95; 95% CI: 0.74-1.23).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Confirms that urgent angiography is not needed for survival benefit in shockable arrest without ST elevation, relevant to invasive management after arrest.

title: Ultrasound-Facilitated, Catheter-Directed Fibrinolysis for Acute Pulmonary Embolism.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Multinational adaptive-design randomised trial with blinded adjudication; 544 patients (273 intervention, 271 control).
appraisal.main_limitation: Effect driven mainly by cardiorespiratory decompensation or collapse, with a 7-day horizon and numerically more major bleeding.
appraisal.one_line: Ultrasound-facilitated catheter-directed fibrinolysis plus anticoagulation reduced early clinical deterioration in intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary-outcome event in 11 patients (4.0%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.3 to 7.1) vs 28 (10.3%; 95% CI, 7.2 to 14.5) (relative risk, 0.39; 95% CI, 0.20 to 0.77; P = 0.005).
appraisal.why_it_matters: First randomised evidence of clinical benefit for catheter-directed therapy in intermediate-risk PE.

title: Left Ventricular Unloading in High-Risk Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 300 patients (148 microaxial flow pump, 152 standard care).
appraisal.main_limitation: Modest sample size and open-label design; wide interval around mortality.
appraisal.one_line: Elective microaxial flow pump unloading did not improve a hierarchical composite in high-risk PCI with severe LV dysfunction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: 36.6% of pairwise comparisons favored the microaxial flow pump, and 43.0% favored standard care (win ratio, 0.85; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.63 to 1.15; P = 0.30).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Argues against routine elective MCS in complex PCI and bears on a numerically higher death count (hazard ratio, 1.54; 95% CI, 0.99 to 2.41).

title: Left Ventricular Unloading in Anterior ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Without Shock: The ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Door to Unload Randomized Controlled Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial (STEMI-DTU); 527 patients (262 treatment, 265 control).
appraisal.main_limitation: Surrogate infarct-size endpoint, with longer total ischemic time in the treatment arm.
appraisal.one_line: Microaxial pump unloading with delayed PCI did not reduce infarct size in anterior STEMI without shock and increased bleeding and vascular complications.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: IS/LVM was 30.8% ± 16.2% in the treatment group and 31.9% ± 16.9% in the control group (mean difference: -1.1%; 95% CI: -4.2 to 2.0; P = 0.50).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Does not support routine unloading before reperfusion in haemodynamically stable anterior STEMI.

title: Standard-dose unfractionated heparin versus low-dose unfractionated heparin and low-molecular-weight heparin in extracorporeal life support (RATE): an open-label, randomised, non-inferiority trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial (RATE); 330 patients enrolled, 110 per arm, 320 analysed at 6 months.
appraisal.main_limitation: Mixed ECLS population with a composite of bleeding and thrombotic outcomes and wide intervals.
appraisal.one_line: Low-dose UFH and LMWH were non-inferior to standard-dose UFH in patients on extracorporeal life support.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Composite primary outcome in 87 (81%) of 107 with standard-dose UFH, 78 (72%) of 108 with low-dose UFH (absolute risk difference -9·1 percentage points [95% CI -20·3 to 2·1]), and 79 (75%) of 105 with LMWH (-6·1 percentage points [-17·2 to 5·0]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: First randomised evidence on anticoagulation intensity in ECMO.

title: Development and Validation of an Adult Medical Urgency Score for US Donor Heart Allocation.

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry-based observational study; training (n = 21 859), validation (n = 7897) and test (n = 8256) datasets.
appraisal.main_limitation: Allocation performance rests on a simulation of waitlist reordering rather than prospective use.
appraisal.one_line: A registry-based score for US donor heart allocation that ranks candidates by medical urgency, including mechanical circulatory support.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: US-CRS had similar or significantly higher time-dependent AUC than the current 6-status system (mean AUC, 0.807 vs 0.693, respectively); first-candidate 6-week transplant-censored mortality was 11.2% (95% CI, 10.1%-12.5%) under the current system and 15.7% (95% CI, 13.9%-17.6%) under the US-CRS-based system.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Device-based urgency in advanced heart failure and shock bears on how mechanical support is used as a bridge.

title: Acute Coronary Occlusions in NSTEMI Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: Insights From the CathPCI Registry.

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry cohort from the CathPCI Registry; 1,198,544 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: In-hospital outcomes only, and occlusion is defined from angiography after the event.
appraisal.one_line: A national registry analysis finds acute coronary occlusion in a sizeable share of NSTEMI patients undergoing PCI, with worse in-hospital outcomes than NSTEMI without occlusion.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Patients with NSTEMI-ACO had a higher risk for the primary composite compared with those with NSTEMI-no-ACO (adjusted OR: 2.26; 95% CI: 2.18-2.34; P < 0.001) but a lower risk compared with those with STEMI (adjusted OR: 0.54; 95% CI: 0.52-0.56; P < 0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It quantifies the population targeted by occlusion-based triage proposals.

title: Intraprocedural Cardiac Arrest in Patients Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Interventions in the United States: An Analysis of the NCDR CathPCI Registry.

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry cohort from the CathPCI Registry, 2018 to 2023; 36,755 intraprocedural cardiac arrests among 3,956,840 PCIs.
appraisal.main_limitation: Descriptive registry data with in-hospital outcomes only.
appraisal.one_line: A national registry describes the incidence and mortality of cardiac arrest during PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A total of 36,755 IPCA occurred during 3,956,840 PCIs (0.93%); In-hospital death occurred in 40.5% of patients with IPCA.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It gives contemporary benchmarks for a catastrophic procedural complication that is rising in incidence.

title: Temporary mechanical circulatory support in cardiogenic shock.

appraisal.design_and_n: Clinical consensus statement; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Expert consensus built on a small number of randomised trials in a heterogeneous syndrome.
appraisal.one_line: EAPCI and ACVC clinical consensus statement updating the 2020 document on temporary mechanical circulatory support in acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Sets contemporary guidance on device selection, escalation, de-escalation and shock team systems after recent microaxial pump and VA-ECMO trials.

title: Adoption of intravascular imaging-guided percutaneous coronary intervention in the United States (2012-2022): temporal trends, disparities, and mortality association.

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective analysis of 5,220,590 PCI admissions from the National Inpatient Sample.
appraisal.main_limitation: Administrative coding captures imaging use imperfectly and confounding by indication cannot be excluded.
appraisal.one_line: US national inpatient analysis of intravascular imaging use in PCI from 2012 to 2022, with adjusted in-hospital mortality comparison.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: IVI-guided PCI increased from 7.1% (2012) to 21.3% (2022) (p trend < 0.001). IVI remained significantly associated with lower odds of in-hospital mortality (aOR 0.783, 95% CI 0.742-0.827; P < 0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Quantifies slow uptake of a guideline-endorsed technique and hospital-level variation.

title: Acute heart failure in emergency settings

appraisal.design_and_n: Consensus document; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Expert consensus with practical advice rather than new comparative evidence; cardiogenic shock is one of four phenotypes covered.
appraisal.one_line: Consensus document on diagnosis, treatment and disposition of acute heart failure in prehospital and emergency department settings, including cardiogenic shock phenotyping.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Sets out early phenotypic triage and research priorities that bear on shock recognition and escalation in the emergency pathway.
